title: The Home page, round 4 — three new chip directions, and the Climate page

steps.path: Pages → Home, the top of the page
steps.headline: Which of these three new directions should the top of the Home page take?
steps.notice: These are three different shapes, not one card restyled. All open the same pages; Everything off is gone from the top, as you asked.
steps.risk: Whichever you pick can still be tuned; if none is right, say what is closest.

variants.label: Small pills
variants.summary: One quiet row of rounded pills, like Apple Home's status bar: an icon and a few words ("5 on", "2 playing", "77° · 74° in", "4 to fix"). A pill takes its colour when something is on: the lights' colour, the app's, the temperature's, red for problems.
variants.risk: The least room for detail: "in 3 rooms" and "1 not responding" only show when you hover.

variants.label: One sentence
variants.summary: The house in one line of words: "5 lights on in 3 rooms · 2 playing · 77° clear outside · 4 problems to fix". Each part is underlined in its colour and opens its page.
variants.risk: Reads beautifully, but it is text: it looks less like something to press than the other two.

variants.label: Big tiles
variants.summary: Four big squares, the number first (5, 3, 77°, 4) with what it means under it, an icon in the corner and a soft blob of its colour behind. Bars bounce on Media while something plays; Problems has a pulsing red dot when urgent.
variants.risk: Takes the most height, pushing the rooms further down.

steps.headline: The thermostat leads the Climate page: a big dial filled to the setting in the mode's colour, big − and +, and the modes as one switch.
steps.changed: Your note: most homes have one thermostat, so it should be prominent. The dial shows the setting in the middle, "Cooling to" above it and "Now 74°" below; the dot on the ring is the room's temperature now. The weather sits beside it.
steps.notice: A second thermostat, if you ever add one, shows as a normal card under these.
steps.risk: Your real thermostat is Nest, so until Nest is signed in it shows as not responding, with that reason.

steps.headline: Chip pages now start with a round back button, the page's icon, a larger title, and what is happening under it.
steps.changed: Your note: the back button and headers needed restyling. The old small "‹ Home" text button is now a round button; the title is larger with its icon beside it.
steps.notice: The same header is used on every chip's page and on Page settings.
steps.risk: The round button has no word on it; hovering says "Back to Home".
